mainTopic: The names and timing of the rains יורה and מלקוש, and the dates of the first rainfall.
overview: The amud opens with the end of a story: רבי יצחק blesses רב נחמן that his children should be like him. The גמרא then returns to rain and explains why the first rain is called יורה and the last rain מלקוש, showing from the פסוקים that both are rains of blessing. Next, ברייתות fix the months of these rains: יורה in מרחשון and מלקוש in ניסן, with three explanations of the name מלקוש in between. רבי מאיר and the חכמים disagree about whether the יורה is in מרחשון or כסלו, and רב חסדא identifies the חכמים as רבי יוסי. A ברייתא lists three sets of dates for the first rainfall, and רבי יוסי's are the latest, ending at ראש חודש כסלו. רב חסדא rules like רבי יוסי, though אמימר reports that his ruling was about when we start asking for rain. The amud ends by asking what the second rainfall is for. רבי זירא answers that it matters for vows, and the משנה he brings continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The blessing: may your children be like you
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק finishes the tree parable and blesses רב נחמן that his offspring should be like him.
steps.simpleTranslation: [May all the saplings planted from you] be like you. So too with you: with what shall I bless you? If with Torah, you already have Torah. If with wealth, you already have wealth. If with children, you already have children. Rather, may it be God's will that your offspring be like you.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of a story. רבי יצחק applies his tree parable to רב נחמן and gives him the one blessing he still can.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the parable, the tree already had sweet fruit, shade and water, so the only blessing left was that its saplings would be like it. רב נחמן already has תורה, wealth and children, so the fitting blessing is that his children will be like him.

keyTerms.meaning: With what shall I bless you?
Your offspring (literally, the offspring of your body)

steps.whatToRemember: When a person already has everything, the best blessing is that his children will be like him.

phrases.english: ...be like you.
phrases.notes: This finishes the tree's blessing from the story just before: may all the saplings planted from you be like you.

phrases.english: So too with you: with what shall I bless you?
If with Torah, you already have Torah;
if with wealth, you already have wealth;
if with children, you already have children.
Rather: may it be [God's] will
that your offspring be like you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף אַתָּה, בַּמָּה אֲבָרֶכְךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story about רב נחמן and רבי יצחק from the previous section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יצחק blesses רב נחמן that his children will be like him.

steps.title: First meaning of יורה: it instructs people
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that the first rain is called יורה because it teaches people to get ready for the rainy season.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: יורה is called that because it instructs people to plaster their roofs, bring in their produce, and take care of all their needs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the topic of rain and quotes a ברייתא. It explains the name יורה as coming from 'teaching' (מורה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word יורה sounds like מורה, 'teacher'. The first rain acts as a signal: winter is coming, so fix your roof and bring your crops inside.

keyTerms.meaning: The first rain of the season

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
'Yoreh' is called that because it instructs people
phrases.notes: The word comes from דברים 11:14, 'יורה ומלקוש', the first rain and the last rain.

phrases.english: to plaster their roofs,
to bring in their produce,
and to take care of all their needs.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יוֹרֶה שֶׁמּוֹרֶה אֶת הַבְּרִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and returns to the main topic of rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יורה means the rain that tells people to prepare for winter.

steps.title: Second meaning of יורה: it soaks the earth
steps.stepSummary: Another explanation: יורה soaks the ground deeply, supported by a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: it soaks the earth and waters it down to the depths, as it says: 'Soaking its furrows, settling its ridges, You soften it with showers, You bless its growth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second reason for the name יורה. Here it connects to 'soaking' (מרוה) and brings a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explanation links יורה to the idea of watering the ground deeply. The פסוק describes rain soaking the furrows and softening the soil, which shows rain that waters thoroughly.

keyTerms.meaning: The deep places under the ground

phrases.english: Another explanation: because it soaks the earth
and waters it down to the depths,
as it says:
'Soaking its furrows, settling its ridges,'
'You soften it with showers, You bless its growth.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: שֶׁמַּרְוֶה אֶת הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, different reason for the name יורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יורה means the rain that soaks the ground deeply.

steps.title: Third meaning of יורה: it falls gently
steps.stepSummary: A third explanation: יורה is rain that comes down gently, not violently.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: יורה means that it comes down gently and does not come down in fury.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a third reason for the name: יורה is related to 'coming down' (יורד), and it comes down softly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three explanations describe יורה as a good rain. This third one sets up the next step, where the ברייתא asks whether יורה might really be a harmful rain.

phrases.english: Another explanation: 'Yoreh' means that it comes down gently
and does not come down in fury.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: יוֹרֶה שֶׁיּוֹרֵד בְּנַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third explanation of the name יורה.

steps.title: Maybe יורה is a destructive rain
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that יורה might mean a harmful rain that knocks off fruit and washes away seeds and trees.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps יורה does not mean that, but rather a rain that knocks the fruit off, washes away the seeds, and washes away the trees?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a worry. Maybe the word יורה describes a violent, damaging rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word יורה can also mean 'shooting', like shooting arrows. That would make it a rain that strikes hard and destroys crops, the opposite of the gentle rain just described.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps it is not so

phrases.english: Or perhaps 'yoreh' does not mean that,
phrases.notes: The worry is that יורה could mean 'shooting,' like shooting arrows, so a rain that strikes hard.

phrases.english: but rather a rain that knocks the fruit off,
washes away the seeds,
and washes away the trees?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ אֵינוֹ יוֹרֶה, אֶלָּא שֶׁמַּשִּׁיר אֶת הַפֵּירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the positive readings of יורה are correct.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that יורה is a rain of blessing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word itself could mean a damaging, hard-hitting rain.

steps.title: מלקוש shows that יורה is a blessing
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק pairs יורה with מלקוש. Since מלקוש is a blessing, יורה must be a blessing too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse teaches: מלקוש. Just as מלקוש is for blessing, so too יורה is for blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the worry by pointing to the word right next to יורה in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two words listed together in the same פסוק are understood the same way. If מלקוש is a good rain, then its partner יורה is also a good rain.

keyTerms.meaning: The late rain at the end of the season

phrases.english: The verse teaches: 'malkosh'.
Just as malkosh is for blessing,
so too yoreh is for blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: מַלְקוֹשׁ, מָה מַלְקוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the worry of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Learning one word from the word paired with it in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יורה might be a destructive rain.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because יורה is paired with מלקוש, a rain of blessing, יורה is also a blessing.

steps.title: Maybe מלקוש is a destructive rain
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא now asks whether מלקוש itself might be harmful, knocking down houses and trees and bringing locusts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps מלקוש does not mean that, but rather a rain that knocks down houses, breaks trees, and brings up locusts?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא turns the same worry onto מלקוש. Maybe it is the dangerous rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 6 assumed מלקוש is a blessing. Now that assumption is questioned, so the proof for יורה is shaken.

phrases.english: Or perhaps 'malkosh' does not mean that,
but rather a rain that knocks down the houses,
breaks the trees,
and brings up the locusts?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ אֵינוֹ מַלְקוֹשׁ, אֶלָּא שֶׁמַּפִּיל אֶת הַבָּתִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption that step 6 relied on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that מלקוש is a blessing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מלקוש could describe a violent rain that causes damage.

steps.title: יורה shows that מלקוש is a blessing
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers the other way around: since יורה is a blessing, so is מלקוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse teaches: יורה. Just as יורה is for blessing, so too מלקוש is for blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא uses יורה to prove that מלקוש is good, the reverse of step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word now proves the other. This sounds circular, and the next step asks exactly that: what proves at least one of them on its own?
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the proof is finished here. Each word is being proven from the other, so the גמרא still needs an outside source, which it gives in the next steps.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: 'yoreh'.
Just as yoreh is for blessing,
so too malkosh is for blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: יוֹרֶה, מָה יוֹרֶה לִבְרָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 by reversing the comparison from step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Learning one word from the word paired with it in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מלקוש might be a destructive rain.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because מלקוש is paired with יורה, a rain of blessing, מלקוש is also a blessing.

steps.title: How do we know יורה itself is a blessing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for an independent source that יורה is a blessing, so the proof is not circular.
steps.simpleTranslation: And יורה itself, from where do we know [that it is for blessing]?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices the circle: each word was proven from the other. It asks for an outside proof for יורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we can prove from somewhere else that יורה is a blessing, then מלקוש is also proven through step 8. This step sets up the answer in the next step.

phrases.english: And yoreh itself, from where do we know [that it is for blessing]?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיוֹרֶה גּוּפֵיהּ מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out that steps 6 and 8 depend on each other and asks for an outside source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: An independent source showing that יורה is a rain of blessing.

steps.title: The פסוק in יואל shows יורה is a blessing
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in יואל says God gave the מורה (first rain) 'for kindness', proving it is a blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Children of Zion, be glad and rejoice in ה׳ your God, for He has given you the first rain for kindness, and He brought down rain for you, the first rain and the late rain, in the first month.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a פסוק that calls the first rain a gift of kindness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls the first rain מורה, the same idea as יורה, and says it was given לצדקה, 'for kindness'. That proves on its own that יורה is a blessing, and through step 8 מלקוש is a blessing too.

keyTerms.meaning: For kindness, as a good gift

steps.whatToRemember: Both יורה and מלקוש are rains of blessing. יורה is proven from the פסוק in יואל, and מלקוש is learned from יורה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It ends a circular proof by finding one firm source. With that one source, the whole pair is proven.

phrases.english: As it is written:
'Children of Zion, be glad and rejoice'
'in ה׳ your God,'

phrases.aramaic: כִּי נָתַן לָכֶם אֶת הַמּוֹרֶה לִצְדָקָה
phrases.english: 'for He has given you the first rain for kindness,'
'and He brought down rain for you,'
'the first rain and the late rain, in the first month.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: וּבְנֵי צִיּוֹן גִּילוּ וְשִׂמְחוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in יואל says the first rain was given 'for kindness', so יורה is a blessing.

steps.title: A ברייתא sets the months of the first and last rain
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states that the יורה falls in מרחשון and the מלקוש in ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: The first rain is in מרחשון, and the last rain is in ניסן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that gives the months when the first and last rains fall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was whether יורה and מלקוש are good or bad. Now the topic moves to timing: which month each rain belongs to.

keyTerms.meaning: The first rain of the season
The last rain of the season
The month after תשרי, in the autumn

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
The first rain is in Marcheshvan, and the last rain is in Nisan.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יוֹרֶה בִּמְרַחְשְׁוָן, וּמַלְקוֹשׁ בְּנִיסָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from whether the rains are a blessing to when they fall.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יורה falls in מרחשון; מלקוש falls in ניסן.

steps.title: Maybe the rains come one month earlier?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the rains might instead be in תשרי and אייר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say the first rain is in מרחשון and the last rain in ניסן? Or maybe the first rain is in תשרי and the last rain in אייר?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises another possible schedule. This sets up the proof from a פסוק that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other option moves both rains: the first rain one month earlier (תשרי) and the last rain one month later (אייר). The ברייתא needs a source to rule this out.

keyTerms.meaning: You say (opens a 'maybe it is otherwise' question)
The month of ראש השנה, before מרחשון

phrases.aramaic: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר: יוֹרֶה בִּמְרַחְשְׁוָן וּמַלְקוֹשׁ בְּנִיסָן,
phrases.english: Do you say the first rain is in Marcheshvan and the last rain in Nisan,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא יוֹרֶה בְּתִשְׁרִי וּמַלְקוֹשׁ בְּאִיָּיר?
phrases.english: or perhaps it is only: the first rain in Tishrei and the last rain in Iyar?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר: יוֹרֶה בִּמְרַחְשְׁוָן וּמַלְקוֹשׁ בְּנִיסָן, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a source for step 11 by raising another schedule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why not say the rains are in תשרי and אייר?

steps.title: The פסוק says 'in its time'
steps.stepSummary: The word 'בעתו' shows that each rain has its proper, fixed time: מרחשון and ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'in its time.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with the word 'בעתו' from the פסוק, which proves that the rains come at their proper time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'In its time' means the time that is best for the crops. Rain in מרחשון helps the seeds sprout, and rain in ניסן finishes the growing. תשרי and אייר are not those times.

phrases.english: The verse states: "In its time."

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״בְּעִתּוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'בעתו' means the proper season, which is מרחשון and ניסן.

steps.title: שמואל explains the name מלקוש
steps.stepSummary: שמואל reads מלקוש as 'מל קש': it cuts away the stubbornness of ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: מלקוש: רב נהילאי בר אידי said in the name of שמואל: It is something that cuts away the stubbornness of ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the last rain is called מלקוש, and gives שמואל's explanation first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל splits the word into מל (cuts away, like ברית מילה) and קש (hard or stubborn). The idea is that the last rain softens the people's hard hearts.

phrases.english: "Malkosh": Rav Nehilai bar Idi said
that Shmuel said:
It is something that cuts away the stubbornness of Israel.
phrases.notes: A play on the word: מַל (cuts away) + קוֹשׁ (hardness).

steps.triggerLanguage: ״מַלְקוֹשׁ״ — אָמַר רַב נְהִילַאי בַּר אִידֵּי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the timing of מלקוש to the meaning of its name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מלקוש = מל + קש: it cuts away ישראל's stubbornness.

steps.title: דבי רבי ישמעאל: it fills the grain in its stalks
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל read מלקוש as 'ממלא' + 'קש': it fills the grain inside its stalks.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: It is something that fills the grain in its stalks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second explanation of the name מלקוש, this one about farming.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here מל comes from ממלא (fills) and קש means the stalks. The last rain makes the grain swell and fill out its stalks.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
It is something that fills the grain in its stalks.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל תָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate explanation of the word מלקוש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מלקוש = ממלא + קש: it fills the grain in its stalks.

steps.title: A ברייתא: it falls on the ears and the stalks
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads מלקוש as 'מלילות' + 'קשין': rain that falls on the ears of grain and on the stalks.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: It is something that comes down on the ears of grain and on the stalks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third explanation of the name מלקוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time מל stands for מלילות (ears of grain) and קש for קשין (stalks). The name describes what the rain lands on.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: There are three explanations of מלקוש: it softens ישראל's hearts (שמואל), it fills the grain (דבי רבי ישמעאל), and it falls on the ears and stalks (a ברייתא).

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר שֶׁיּוֹרֵד עַל הַמְּלִילוֹת וְעַל הַקַּשִּׁין.
phrases.english: It is something that comes down on the ears of grain and on the stalks.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third explanation of the word מלקוש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מלקוש = מלילות + קשין: it falls on the ears and the stalks.

steps.title: Another ברייתא with the same months
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא opens with the same rule: יורה in מרחשון, מלקוש in ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: The first rain is in מרחשון, and the last rain is in ניסן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different ברייתא that starts with the same rule. This sets up a new question about the first rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is the same as in step 11, but this ברייתא will test a different option: not an earlier month, but a later one (כסלו).

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
The first rain is in Marcheshvan, and the last rain is in Nisan.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יוֹרֶה בִּמְרַחְשְׁוָן, וּמַלְקוֹשׁ בְּנִיסָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the timing of the rains, using a new ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יורה in מרחשון, מלקוש in ניסן.

steps.title: Maybe the first rain is in כסלו?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the יורה might really belong in כסלו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say the first rain is in מרחשון, or maybe it is only in the month of כסלו?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a later month as a possible time for the first rain. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the challenge is only about the יורה, and it pushes the date later instead of earlier. The ברייתא needs to show why מרחשון is right.

phrases.english: Do you say the first rain is in Marcheshvan,
or perhaps it is only in the month of Kislev?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בְּחֹדֶשׁ כִּסְלֵיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the date in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is the יורה in מרחשון and not כסלו?

steps.title: Comparing the first rain to the last rain
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק puts 'בעתו' next to both rains. Rain after ניסן is no blessing, so the מלקוש has a strict time. The same is true for the יורה, so it must be in מרחשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'in its time, the first rain and the last rain.' Just as the last rain has its exact time, so does the first rain. Once ניסן is over, rain that falls is not a sign of blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers by comparing the two rains, which the פסוק mentions together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know the מלקוש has a firm deadline: rain after ניסן is not a blessing. Since the פסוק links the two rains, the יורה also has a firm, exact time and should not slip later into כסלו.

phrases.english: The verse states: "In its time, the first rain and the last rain,"
just as the last rain is in its time,
so too the first rain is in its time;
once Nisan is over
and rains fall, it is not a sign of blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״בְּעִתּוֹ יוֹרֶה וּמַלְקוֹשׁ״, מָה מַלְקוֹשׁ בְּעִתּוֹ — אַף יוֹרֶה בְּעִתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the כסלו question in step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The יורה is compared to the מלקוש, whose time is fixed (rain after ניסן is no blessing). So the יורה also has a fixed time, which is מרחשון.

steps.title: רבי מאיר and the חכמים disagree
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא shows that 'מרחשון' is the view of רבי מאיר, while the חכמים put the יורה in כסלו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: The first rain is in מרחשון and the last rain is in ניסן. These are the words of רבי מאיר. The חכמים say: The first rain is in כסלו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא showing that the date of the first rain is a מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ברייתות followed רבי מאיר. The חכמים disagree and say the יורה is in כסלו, which is the very option that step 18 raised.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: the יורה is in מרחשון. חכמים: the יורה is in כסלו. Both agree the מלקוש is in ניסן.
steps.confusionAlert: The earlier ברייתא that said 'not כסלו' follows רבי מאיר. The חכמים do say כסלו.

phrases.english: Another baraita teaches:
The first rain is in Marcheshvan and the last rain is in Nisan;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Rabbis say: The first rain is in Kislev.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ: יוֹרֶה בִּמְרַחְשְׁוָן וּמַלְקוֹשׁ בְּנִיסָן, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the מרחשון view is רבי מאיר's, and that the חכמים disagree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: יורה in מרחשון. חכמים: יורה in כסלו.

steps.title: Who are these חכמים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא is behind the view of the חכמים who put the יורה in כסלו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who are the חכמים?
steps.whatsHappening: The last ברייתא quoted an unnamed group, the חכמים, who said the יורה comes in כסלו. Now the גמרא wants to know which named תנא holds that view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a ברייתא says just 'חכמים', the גמרא often tries to find out which specific תנא it means. Knowing the name lets us link this view to his other rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, an unnamed group of תנאים

phrases.english: Who are the Sages?
phrases.notes: He means the חכמים from the last ברייתא, who put the יורה in כסלו.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the identity of the חכמים quoted in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which named תנא holds that the יורה is in כסלו.

steps.title: It is רבי יוסי: the three views on the first rainfall
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the חכמים are רבי יוסי, and brings a ברייתא where three תנאים give dates for the first rainfall. רבי יוסי's dates are the latest and end at ראש חודש כסלו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is רבי יוסי, as a ברייתא teaches: When is the first rainfall? Early: the 3rd of מרחשון. Middle: the 7th. Late: the 17th. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: the 7th, the 17th and the 23rd. רבי יוסי says: the 17th, the 23rd and ראש חודש כסלו.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers that the חכמים are רבי יוסי. He proves it from a ברייתא where רבי יוסי gives the latest dates of everyone for the first rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each תנא gives three dates: an early one, a middle one and a late one. רבי מאיר starts on the 3rd of מרחשון, רבי יהודה on the 7th, and רבי יוסי on the 17th. Only רבי יוסי's range reaches ראש חודש כסלו, so he matches the חכמים who said the יורה can be in כסלו.

keyTerms.meaning: The first rainfall of the season

steps.confusionAlert: These are not three different rains. Each תנא is giving three possible dates for the same first rainfall: early, middle and late.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא,
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: It is Rabbi Yosei,
as it is taught: When is the first rainfall?
The early one is on the third of Marcheshvan,
the middle one on the seventh of it,
the late one on the seventeenth of it,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says: On the seventh,
and on the seventeenth, and on the twenty-third.
Rabbi Yosei says: On the seventeenth,
and on the twenty-third, and on the New Moon of Kislev.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים are רבי יוסי, whose latest date for the first rainfall is ראש חודש כסלו.
steps.whyThisMatters: These dates matter in practice: they decide when the rain is counted as late, which affects when people begin fasting for rain.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: individuals do not fast before ראש חודש כסלו
steps.stepSummary: Following his dates, רבי יוסי rules that the יחידים do not start fasting for rain until ראש חודש כסלו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so רבי יוסי used to say: The individuals do not fast until ראש חודש כסלו arrives.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds another ruling of רבי יוסי that follows from his dates. Special individuals do not begin fasting for rain before ראש חודש כסלו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יוסי says the first rain can come as late as ראש חודש כסלו, there is no drought yet before that date. So even the people who fast earliest have no reason to fast before then.

keyTerms.meaning: And likewise; this ruling fits the earlier one
Special individuals, people who fast for rain before the rest of the community

phrases.english: And so Rabbi Yosei would say:
The individuals do not fast
phrases.notes: These are the special people who start fasting for rain earlier than everyone else.

phrases.english: until the New Moon of Kislev arrives.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with a practical result of רבי יוסי's late dates.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Individuals do not fast for rain before ראש חודש כסלו.

steps.title: רב חסדא rules like רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives a final ruling: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי's dates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This means we use רבי יוסי's later dates. In practice, the rain is not counted as late, and individuals do not fast, before ראש חודש כסלו.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
The halacha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the views in the ברייתא of steps 22-23.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי on the dates of the first rainfall.

steps.title: אמימר's version: רב חסדא ruled about asking for rain
steps.stepSummary: אמימר teaches רב חסדא's ruling differently. It was said about when we start asking for rain: the תנא קמא says the 3rd of מרחשון, רבן גמליאל says the 7th, and רב חסדא rules like רבן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר taught this statement of רב חסדא in this way: On the 3rd of מרחשון we ask for rain. רבן גמליאל says: On the 7th. רב חסדא said: The הלכה follows רבן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר gives a different version of where רב חסדא said his ruling. In his version, the ruling was about when we start asking for rain, and it follows רבן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רב חסדא ruled like רבי יוסי on the dates of the first rainfall. In אמימר's version, his ruling was on a different argument: whether we start asking for rain on the 3rd or the 7th of מרחשון. There he rules like רבן גמליאל, who says the 7th.

keyTerms.meaning: In this wording, in this version
We ask for rain (in our prayers)

steps.confusionAlert: אמימר does not argue about the הלכה himself. He is reporting a different version of what רב חסדא said and which argument he was ruling on.

phrases.english: Ameimar would teach this statement of Rav Chisda
in this wording:
On the third of Marcheshvan we ask for rain,
Rabban Gamliel says: On the seventh of it,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל.
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: The halacha is in accordance with Rabban Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמֵּימָר מַתְנֵי לְהָא דְּרַב חִסְדָּא בְּהָא לִישָּׁנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of רב חסדא's ruling from step 24, placing it on a different argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In אמימר's version, רב חסדא rules like רבן גמליאל that we start asking for rain on the 7th of מרחשון.
steps.whyThisMatters: This affects when we begin asking for rain in our prayers in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Whose view is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's rule about seven days of rain?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: rain that falls seven days in a row counts as two rainfalls. It asks which תנא this ברייתא follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does this ברייתא follow? רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Rains that fell seven days in a row, you count them as the first and second rainfall, or as the second and third.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new ברייתא about seven days of nonstop rain and asks whose view it matches. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says one long week of rain can count as two of the rainfalls. That only makes sense with a view where the rainfalls are about a week apart. So the גמרא wants to know which of the three תנאים from step 22 he follows.

keyTerms.meaning: One after another, in a row

phrases.english: Whose view does that which is taught follow?
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: גְּשָׁמִים שֶׁיָּרְדוּ שִׁבְעָה יָמִים זֶה אַחַר זֶה
phrases.english: Rains that fell seven days one after another,
you count them as
the first and second rainfall, or the second and third,

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the three views of step 22 to place a new ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of the three תנאים about the first rainfall does רבן שמעון בן גמליאל follow?

steps.title: It follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ברייתא follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view? רבי יוסי's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: this ברייתא goes with רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's dates (the 17th, the 23rd, ראש חודש כסלו) are each about a week apart. So seven days of rain can stretch from one of his dates to the next and count as two rainfalls. The other תנאים do not have this steady one-week gap: רבי מאיר's dates are 4 and then 10 days apart, and רבי יהודה's are 10 and then 6 days apart.

phrases.english: Whose view? Rabbi Yosei's.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן — כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל follows רבי יוסי, whose dates are about a week apart.

steps.title: רב חסדא again rules like רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The section closes with רב חסדא's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's rule fits רבי יוסי, ruling like רבי יוסי also means we accept the rule about seven days of rain. A week of rain in a row counts as two rainfalls.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three views on the dates of the first rainfall. רבי יוסי's are the latest and end at ראש חודש כסלו, and רב חסדא rules like him. In אמימר's version, רב חסדא's ruling was about asking for rain, and it follows רבן גמליאל (the 7th of מרחשון).

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
The halacha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a final ruling after placing the ברייתא with רבי יוסי.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי, including the rule that seven days of rain in a row count as two rainfalls.

steps.title: What is the second rainfall used for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that the first and third rainfalls have clear practical uses, and asks what practical use the second rainfall has.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that the first rainfall is mentioned, since that is when we start asking for rain. The third rainfall is mentioned because that is when we start fasting. But the second rainfall, what is it for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we need to know the date of the second rainfall at all. It points out that the first and third rainfalls each have an obvious use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בשלמא means 'it makes sense that,' and the גמרא uses it to agree with the easy cases first. The first rainfall marks when we begin asking for rain, and the third marks when we start fasting if rain has not come. The second rainfall seems to have no job, so the גמרא asks what it is for.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense that / granted (the גמרא accepts one part before questioning another)
A rainfall; here, one of the three fixed times for the rainy season

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an attack on the ברייתא. The גמרא is not saying the second rainfall shouldn't be mentioned. It just wants to know what practical difference that date makes.

phrases.english: Granted, the first rainfall is for asking [for rain].
The third is for fasting.
The second, for what?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא רְבִיעָה רִאשׁוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling whose opinion the rainfall dates follow, the גמרא now asks what practical use each rainfall date has, focusing on the second.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What halachic difference depends on the date of the second rainfall?

steps.title: רבי זירא: The second rainfall matters for vows
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that the second rainfall matters for נדרים, and introduces a משנה to prove it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: The second rainfall matters for vows, as we learned in a משנה:
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the question: the second rainfall matters for the laws of vows. He is setting up the next move by starting to quote a משנה that will show how.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer gives the second rainfall a job: it is linked to the laws of נדרים. The word דתנן tells us a משנה is coming as the source. The details of how vows connect to the rainfall will appear in that משנה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
For vows, as we learned [in a mishna]:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: לִנְדָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 29 about the purpose of the second rainfall.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second rainfall's date matters for the laws of vows, as shown in a משנה that is about to be quoted.
